label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 12
knowledgePattern: Group logically equivalent quantified claims before selecting a sole truth
solution:
For a fixed a, abbreviate P(a): ∀x>a, f(x)>0 and Q(a): f(a)<0. The negation of P is that some x>a has f(x)≤0. The seven universally quantified options become: A, P⇒Q; B, Q⇒¬P; C, Q⇒P; D, ¬Q⇒¬P; E, P⇒¬Q; F, ¬Q⟺¬P; G, Q⇒¬P.

A and D are contrapositives, so neither can be the only true statement. B, E and G are equivalent, so none can be the only true statement. F is equivalent to P if and only if Q, and would force both A and C to hold. Only C can therefore be the sole truth.

This is consistent: define f(0)=−1 and f(x)=1 for every x≠0. Q holds only at a = 0, and all later values are positive, so C holds for every a. At a = 1, P is true and Q false, disproving A, D and F. At a = 0, Q and P are both true, disproving B, E and G. Answer C.

hints.title: Shorten the two repeated claims
hints.body: Call “positive for every x>a” P, and call “negative at a” Q. Rewrite each option using those two names.
hints.recap: “Only if”, “necessary” and “sufficient” must be translated in the correct direction.
hints.pitfall: Keep the words “for every x greater than a” together as one claim.
hints.pause: Write an implication for each option.

recall.reminder: “Only if”, “necessary” and “sufficient” must be translated in the correct direction.

hints.title: Compare the rules
hints.body: Look for equivalent implications, including contrapositives. If two options always agree, neither can be the only true one.
hints.recap: An implication and its contrapositive have the same truth value.
hints.pitfall: An if-and-only-if contains two directions, so check both.
hints.pause: Use exactly one to eliminate groups that force each other.

recall.reminder: An implication and its contrapositive have the same truth value.
